literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 187 个地区共通报了 886 例 HCPS 病例,平均每年 49.2 例。通知与较高的男性人口比例和森林火灾导致的更大的烧毁面积呈正相关,与城市化和人口密度呈负相关。462名住院患者中,院内病死率为19.7%。年龄较大、女性和土著群体归属与较高的住院 死亡率 风险显着相关,住院时间较短和手术干预次数较多也是如此。 [10.1111/zph.70084]

2019年至2025年共报告1,492例肾综合征出血热(HFRS)病例,平均年度发病率发病率为100,000人中1.073例。发病率在2019年至2021年呈上升趋势(年百分比变化[APC] 40.70%,p=0.103),在2021年至2025年呈下降趋势(APC −13.60%,p=0.052)。多数年份存在空间聚集现象,2021年莫兰指数(Moran’s I)最高为0.438。识别出三个时空聚集区,均集中于2021年秋冬季,最大聚集区覆盖七个县,相对风险为13.56。 [10.3389/fpubh.2026.1868358]

共识支持致病性汉坦病毒通过 αvβ3 整合素进入内皮细胞和血小板,破坏 VEGF-VEGFR2 信号传导并使内皮细胞对生理 VEGF 浓度过敏。CD8+ T 细胞扩增和活化的巨噬细胞释放 TNF-α、IFN-γ 和一氧化氮,增强微血管通透性并导致心肌抑制。尸检研究证实心脏内皮和间质巨噬细胞中存在病毒抗原,直接导致汉坦病毒性心肌炎。血清转化先于临床恶化,保留了 IgM 血清学 的诊断效用。 [10.3390/v18080915]
审查得出的结论是,尽管游轮处于健康定位,但它仍然是疾病 传播 风险最高的环境之一。它强调需要更细致地了解健康促进如何与 暴发 风险相互作用,并表明当前的卫生检查合规性无法可靠地预测或预防 暴发。 [10.3390/tourhosp7080253]

汉坦病毒 越来越被认为是具有重大全球公共卫生影响的新兴人畜共患病原体。该评论强调,旧世界病毒和新世界病毒的传统分类正在变得模糊,因为现在观察到重叠的肾脏和肺部表现。此外,它还指出,已记录了人与人之间的安第斯山脉病毒 传播,病毒在呼吸道分泌物中脱落。该综述还强调,由 VEGF 敏化、Src 激酶和 RhoA 通路激活、周细胞感染和炎症反应失调驱动的内皮功能障碍仍然是严重疾病的标志。 [10.1002/rmv.70191]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: A total of 886 HCPS cases were notified across 187 districts, averaging 49.2 cases per year. Notifications were positively associated with higher male population rates and greater burned area due to forest fires, and negatively associated with urbanization and population density. [10.1111/zph.70084]

A total of 1,492 HFRS cases were reported from 2019 to 2025, with an average annual incidence rate of 1.073 per 100,000 people. The incidence showed an upward trend from 2019 to 2021 (APC 40.70%, p = 0.103) and a downward trend from 2021 to 2025 (APC −13.60%, p = 0.052). [10.3389/fpubh.2026.1868358]

Consensus supports that pathogenic hantaviruses enter endothelial cells and platelets via αvβ3 integrins, disrupting VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling and rendering endothelial cells hypersensitive to physiological VEGF concentrations. [10.3390/v18080915]
The review concludes that cruise ships, despite their wellness positioning, are among the riskiest environments for disease transmission. [10.3390/tourhosp7080253]

Hantaviruses are increasingly recognized as emerging zoonotic pathogens with significant global public health implications. The review highlights that traditional classifications into Old World and New World viruses are becoming blurred, as overlapping renal and pulmonary manifestations are now observed. [10.1002/rmv.70191]

news.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 悬挂荷兰国旗的探险船 MV Hondius 上疑似安第斯菌株汉坦病毒暴发 导致乘客在圣赫勒拿岛下船并进行医疗疏散;调查正在进行中。 [news-ee062519db3332b4]
一名法国旅客从游轮返回后,安第斯山脉汉坦病毒检测呈阳性;该病例已得到法国卫生部长的确认,目前正在接受治疗。 [news-3c70f493c7e4d1b1]
报告了两例疑似汉坦病毒病例:西班牙的一例与一名游轮乘客有关,特里斯坦达库尼亚的一例与同一艘游轮有关。世卫组织确认船上 8 例病例中有 6 例为 汉坦病毒,病原体为安第斯山脉病毒。该事件正在调查中,分为确诊、疑似和可能状态。 [news-97b96c237ebd5c6a]
世卫组织确认了 5 例汉坦病毒病例,与一艘 暴发 游轮有关;另外还有三起疑似病例。世卫组织总干事谭德塞表示,如果迅速有效地实施公共卫生措施,预计 暴发 仍将受到限制。 [news-41a071c92de9bd7f]

papers.title: The Changing Landscape of Hantavirus Infections: A Narrative Review of Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, and Countermeasures.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are emerging zoonotic pathogens of increasing global public health significance. Their epidemiological landscape is rapidly changing due to ecological disruption, climate variability, urbanisation, and evolving human-animal interfaces. This narrative review synthesises current knowledge on hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management, and emerging countermeasures, with a focus on developments from the past 5 years. Traditionally classified into Old World viruses causing haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and New World viruses causing hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), this dichotomy has become increasingly blurred, with overlapping renal and pulmonary manifestations now recognized. Among the most consequential recent advances is the consolidated evidence for person-to-person transmission of Andes virus, documented among household contacts and during the prodromal phase, with viral shedding in respiratory secretions. Endothelial dysfunction remains the pathological hallmark of severe disease, driven by VEGF sensitisation, Src kinase and RhoA pathway activation, pericyte infection, and dysregulated inflammatory responses including IL-6 trans-signalling. Concurrently, environmental and ecological studies have linked climate change, rodent population dynamics, land-use modification, and urbanisation to increased human disease risk across multiple continents. Diagnostic strategies continue to rely on serology and molecular testing, while management remains predominantly supportive, with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improving survival in fulminant HCPS. Importantly, recent structural virology advances have enabled the development of broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies targeting conserved quaternary epitopes, as well as next-generation vaccine platforms including DNA, mRNA, and prefusion-stabilised glycoprotein candidates. Hantaviruses represent a paradigmatic One Health challenge at the intersection of environmental change, viral evolution, and global interconnectedness. Despite major progress in understanding transmission dynamics and endothelial pathogenesis, critical gaps remain regarding determinants of person-to-person spread, long-term post-infection sequelae, and the absence of licenced broadly protective vaccines or specific antiviral therapies. Future preparedness will require integrated surveillance frameworks combining ecological monitoring, genomic epidemiology, and clinical readiness within coordinated international public health strategies.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on hantaviruses, specifically mammalian orthohantaviruses associated with human disease, and their syndromes such as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). The central question is to understand the changing epidemiological landscape, pathogenesis, and countermeasures against hantaviruses, with an emphasis on recent developments over the past 5 years.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of current knowledge on hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management, and emerging countermeasures. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or study counts. The methods section indicates that the review is based on a comprehensive analysis of the literature, with no explicit mention of meta-analysis or systematic review techniques.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Hantaviruses are increasingly recognized as emerging zoonotic pathogens with significant global public health implications. The review highlights that traditional classifications into Old World and New World viruses are becoming blurred, as overlapping renal and pulmonary manifestations are now observed. Additionally, it notes that person-to-person transmission of Andes virus has been documented, with viral shedding in respiratory secretions. The review also underscores that endothelial dysfunction, driven by VEGF sensitisation, Src kinase and RhoA pathway activation, pericyte infection, and dysregulated inflammatory responses, remains the hallmark of severe disease.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There are critical gaps in understanding the determinants of person-to-person spread, long-term post-infection sequelae, and the lack of licensed broadly protective vaccines or specific antiviral therapies. The review also points out that while diagnostic strategies rely on serology and molecular testing, and management remains supportive with ECMO improving survival in fulminant HCPS, there is no consensus on the most effective interventions or surveillance methods.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future preparedness requires integrated surveillance frameworks that combine ecological monitoring, genomic epidemiology, and clinical readiness within coordinated international public health strategies. The review suggests that research should focus on elucidating the mechanisms of person-to-person transmission, long-term sequelae, and the development of broadly protective vaccines and specific antiviral therapies.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the evolving epidemiology, pathogenesis, and countermeasures of hantaviruses, emphasizing their role as emerging zoonotic pathogens. The review highlights the blurring of traditional classifications between Old World and New World hantaviruses, the documented person-to-person transmission of Andes virus, and the persistent endothelial dysfunction as a hallmark of severe disease. Despite advancements in diagnostics and supportive management, significant gaps remain in understanding transmission dynamics, long-term effects, and the absence of effective vaccines or antiviral therapies. The review underscores the need for integrated surveillance and research to address these challenges and improve global public health preparedness.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 汉坦病毒,特别是与人类疾病相关的哺乳动物正汉坦病毒及其综合征,例如 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS)。中心问题是了解不断变化的流行病学格局、发病机制以及针对汉坦病毒的对策,重点是过去5年的最新发展。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对汉坦病毒病毒学、流行病学、发病机制、临床管理和新兴对策的当前知识的叙述性综合。它不报告具体的数据库、搜索日期或研究计数。方法部分表明该综述基于对文献的综合分析,没有明确提及荟萃分析或系统综述技术。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 汉坦病毒 越来越被认为是具有重大全球公共卫生影响的新兴人畜共患病原体。该评论强调,旧世界病毒和新世界病毒的传统分类正在变得模糊,因为现在观察到重叠的肾脏和肺部表现。此外,它还指出,已记录了人与人之间的安第斯山脉病毒 传播,病毒在呼吸道分泌物中脱落。该综述还强调,由 VEGF 敏化、Src 激酶和 RhoA 通路激活、周细胞感染和炎症反应失调驱动的内皮功能障碍仍然是严重疾病的标志。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: This review focuses on hantaviruses, specifically mammalian orthohantaviruses associated with human disease, and their syndromes such as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). The central question is to understand the changing epidemiological landscape, pathogenesis, and countermeasures against hantaviruses, with an emphasis on recent developments over the past 5 years.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of current knowledge on hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management, and emerging countermeasures. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or study counts. The methods section indicates that the review is based on a comprehensive analysis of the literature, with no explicit mention of meta-analysis or systematic review techniques.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Hantaviruses are increasingly recognized as emerging zoonotic pathogens with significant global public health implications. The review highlights that traditional classifications into Old World and New World viruses are becoming blurred, as overlapping renal and pulmonary manifestations are now observed. Additionally, it notes that person-to-person transmission of Andes virus has been documented, with viral shedding in respiratory secretions. The review also underscores that endothelial dysfunction, driven by VEGF sensitisation, Src kinase and RhoA pathway activation, pericyte infection, and dysregulated inflammatory responses, remains the hallmark of severe disease.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There are critical gaps in understanding the determinants of person-to-person spread, long-term post-infection sequelae, and the lack of licensed broadly protective vaccines or specific antiviral therapies. analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Future preparedness requires integrated surveillance frameworks that combine ecological monitoring, genomic epidemiology, and clinical readiness within coordinated international public health strategies. The review suggests that research should focus on elucidating the mechanisms of person-to-person transmission, long-term sequelae, and the development of broadly protective vaccines and specific antiviral therapies.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 感染的变化格局:流行病学、发病机制 和对策的叙述回顾。
papers.source_body_en: Hantaviruses are emerging zoonotic pathogens of increasing global public health significance. Their epidemiological landscape is rapidly changing due to ecological disruption, climate variability, urbanisation, and evolving human-animal interfaces. This narrative review synthesises current knowledge on hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management, and emerging countermeasures, with a focus on developments from the past 5 years. Traditionally classified into Old World viruses causing haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and New World viruses causing hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), this dichotomy has become increasingly blurred, with overlapping renal and pulmonary manifestations now recognized. Among the most consequential recent advances is the consolidated evidence for person-to-person transmission of Andes virus, documented among household contacts and during the prodromal phase, with viral shedding in respiratory secretions. Endothelial dysfunction remains the pathological hallmark of severe disease, driven by VEGF sensitisation, Src kinase and RhoA pathway activation, pericyte infection, and dysregulated inflammatory responses including IL-6 trans-signalling. Concurrently, environmental and ecological studies have linked climate change, rodent population dynamics, land-use modification, and urbanisation to increased human disease risk across multiple continents. Diagnostic strategies continue to rely on serology and molecular testing, while management remains predominantly supportive, with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improving survival in fulminant HCPS. Importantly, recent structural virology advances have enabled the development of broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies targeting conserved quaternary epitopes, as well as next-generation vaccine platforms including DNA, mRNA, and prefusion-stabilised glycoprotein candidates. Hantaviruses represent a paradigmatic One Health challenge at the intersection of environmental change, viral evolution, and global interconnectedness. Despite major progress in understanding transmission dynamics and endothelial pathogenesis, critical gaps remain regarding determinants of person-to-person spread, long-term post-infection sequelae, and the absence of licenced broadly protective vaccines or specific antiviral therapies. Future preparedness will require integrated surveillance frameworks combining ecological monitoring, genomic epidemiology, and clinical readiness within coordinated international public health strategies.

papers.title: Ecological and Individual‐Level Factors Associated With Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome Notifications and in‐Hospital Mortality Among Hospitalized Patients in Chile, 2005–2022
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) is a severe zoonotic disease caused by Orthohantavirus andesense (Andes virus, ANDV), with significant public health burden in Chile. Despite decades of surveillance, knowledge gaps remain regarding the ecological drivers of notification burden and the individual‐level determinants of in‐hospital mortality among hospitalized patients. This study aimed to address both dimensions simultaneously, providing a multilevel characterization of HCPS epidemiology in Chile from 2005 to 2022. Methods Two complementary analyses were conducted. First, an ecological study examined district‐level HCPS notifications (2005–2022) using a negative binomial mixed‐effects model, with predictors including male population rate, urbanization proportion, population density, season and burned area due to forest fires during the most recent summer season. Second, an individual‐level analysis of hospitalized HCPS patients (2010–2020) used a logistic mixed‐effects model to identify correlates of in‐hospital mortality among hospitalized patients, including age, sex, indigenous group affiliation, hospitalization duration and number of surgical interventions. Results A total of 886 HCPS cases were notified across 187 districts, averaging 49.2 cases per year. Notifications were positively associated with higher male population rates and greater burned area due to forest fires, and negatively associated with urbanization and population density. Among 462 hospitalized patients, the in‐hospital case‐fatality ratio was 19.7%. Older age, female sex and indigenous group affiliation were significantly associated with higher in‐hospital mortality risk among hospitalized patients. Shorter hospitalization duration and greater number of surgical interventions, as correlates of clinical severity and complexity, were also associated with in‐hospital mortality among hospitalized patients. Conclusions HCPS notification burden in Chile is shaped by environmental and demographic factors, with forest fire activity representing a novel and actionable ecological risk indicator. In‐hospital mortality among hospitalized patients is disproportionately concentrated in older, female, and indigenous populations, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance, equitable healthcare access and integrated One Health strategies to reduce the burden of HCPS in Chile.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由安第斯正汉坦病毒(安第斯病毒,ANDV)引起的汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS) 在智利造成了重大的公共卫生负担,尽管 监测 已经存在了数十年,但通知负担的生态驱动因素和住院 死亡率 的个人层面决定因素仍然没有得到充分的表征。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究进行了两项补充分析:对 2005 年至 2022 年 HCPS 通知进行的生态区级分析,以及对 2010 年至 2020 年智利住院 HCPS 患者的个人层面分析。
elements_zh.methods: 生态分析使用负二项式混合效应模型来评估 HCPS 通知的地区级预测因素,包括男性人口率、城市化比例、人口密度、季节和森林火灾烧毁面积。个体层面的分析应用逻辑混合效应模型来确定住院患者中 死亡率 的相关性,考虑年龄、性别、土著群体归属、住院时间和手术干预次数。
elements_zh.main_results: 187 个地区共通报了 886 例 HCPS 病例,平均每年 49.2 例。通知与较高的男性人口比例和森林火灾导致的更大的烧毁面积呈正相关,与城市化和人口密度呈负相关。462名住院患者中,院内病死率为19.7%。年龄较大、女性和土著群体归属与较高的住院 死亡率 风险显着相关,住院时间较短和手术干预次数较多也是如此。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,HCPS 通知负担是由环境和人口因素决定的,森林火灾活动正在成为一种新颖且可操作的生态风险指标。他们强调,住院 死亡率 对老年人、女性和土著人群的影响尤为严重,强调需要有针对性的 监测 和公平的医疗服务。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,将森林火灾活动等环境风险指标纳入 监测 系统可以改善 HCPS 的早期发现和预防。该研究还强调了解决医疗保健差异以减少高危人群住院 死亡率 的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖 监测 和医院数据而受到限制,这些数据可能不足以代表轻度或未确诊病例,并且缺乏详细的临床细节。尽管多层次方法加强了因果推理,但由于潜在的不可测量的混杂因素和观察设计,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介汉坦病毒心肺综合征(HCPS)是由安第斯正汉坦病毒(Andesvirus,ANDV)引起的严重人畜共患疾病,给智利带来了重大的公共卫生负担。尽管 监测 已有数十年的历史,但关于通知负担的生态驱动因素以及住院患者住院 死亡率 的个体层面决定因素仍然存在知识差距。本研究旨在同时解决这两个维度,提供 2005 年至 2022 年智利 HCPS 流行病学 的多层次特征。方法 进行了两项互补分析。首先,一项生态研究使用负二项混合效应模型检查了地区级 HCPS 通知(2005-2022 年),预测变量包括男性人口率、城市化比例、人口密度、季节和最近夏季森林火灾造成的烧毁面积。其次,对住院 HCPS 患者(2010-2020 年)进行个体层面分析,使用逻辑混合效应模型来确定住院患者中 死亡率 的相关性,包括年龄、性别、土著群体归属、住院时间和手术干预次数。结果 187 个地区共通报 886 例 HCPS 病例,平均每年 49.2 例。通知与较高的男性人口比例和森林火灾导致的更大的烧毁面积呈正相关,与城市化和人口密度呈负相关。462名住院患者中,院内病死率为19.7%。住院患者中年龄较大、女性和土著群体归属与较高的住院 死亡率 风险显着相关。较短的住院时间和较多的手术干预次数(与临床严重程度和复杂性相关)也与住院患者的住院 死亡率 相关。结论 智利的 HCPS 通知负担由环境和人口因素决定,森林火灾活动代表了一种新颖且可操作的生态风险指标。住院患者中的住院 死亡率 不成比例地集中在老年人、女性和土著人群中,这凸显了需要有针对性的 监测、公平的医疗服务和综合 One Health 战略,以减轻智利 HCPS 的负担。

analysis_zh.methods: 生态分析使用负二项式混合效应模型来评估 HCPS 通知的地区级预测因素,包括男性人口率、城市化比例、人口密度、季节和森林火灾烧毁面积。个体层面的分析应用逻辑混合效应模型来确定住院患者中 死亡率 的相关性,考虑年龄、性别、土著群体归属、住院时间和手术干预次数。
analysis_zh.main_results: 187 个地区共通报了 886 例 HCPS 病例,平均每年 49.2 例。通知与较高的男性人口比例和森林火灾导致的更大的烧毁面积呈正相关,与城市化和人口密度呈负相关。462名住院患者中,院内病死率为19.7%。年龄较大、女性和土著群体归属与较高的住院 死亡率 风险显着相关,住院时间较短和手术干预次数较多也是如此。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,HCPS 通知负担是由环境和人口因素决定的,森林火灾活动正在成为一种新颖且可操作的生态风险指标。他们强调,住院 死亡率 对老年人、女性和土著人群的影响尤为严重,强调需要有针对性的 监测 和公平的医疗服务。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,将森林火灾活动等环境风险指标纳入 监测 系统可以改善 HCPS 的早期发现和预防。该研究还强调了解决医疗保健差异以减少高危人群住院 死亡率 的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖 监测 和医院数据而受到限制,这些数据可能不足以代表轻度或未确诊病例,并且缺乏详细的临床细节。尽管多层次方法加强了因果推理,但由于潜在的不可测量的混杂因素和观察设计,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Cardiopulmonary Failure in Hantavirus Disease: Mechanisms, Recognition, and ECMO-Based Management
papers.abstract: Background: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), also designated hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, is caused by New World hantaviruses, principally Sin Nombre virus in North America and Andes virus in South America. The syndrome is characterized by rapidly progressive noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and myocardial depression, with case fatality rates of 25% to 40%. A 2026 outbreak aboard an expedition cruise ship in the South Atlantic, comprising 13 cases and three deaths, confirmed that Andes virus can be transmitted between humans in a confined setting remote from the rodent reservoir. Methods: Virological, pathophysiological, clinical, and therapeutic aspects of HPS were reviewed, with particular emphasis on cardiopulmonary mechanisms. Sources were identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, with priority given to original research articles, clinical series, and controlled trials published through 2025. Literature published in English and Spanish was included. Results: Pathogenic hantaviruses enter endothelial cells and platelets via αvβ3 integrins, disrupting the VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling axis and rendering endothelial cells hypersensitive to physiological VEGF concentrations. Expansion of CD8+ T cells and activated macrophages releases TNF-alpha, IFN-gamma, and nitric oxide, amplifying microvascular permeability and contributing to myocardial depression. Autopsy studies demonstrate direct hantaviral myocarditis with viral antigen in cardiac endothelium and interstitial macrophages. Transpulmonary thermodilution confirms simultaneous hypovolemia, reduced global ejection fraction, and elevated extravascular lung water. Because the incubation period is long and the cardiopulmonary phase is substantially immune-mediated, seroconversion precedes rather than follows clinical deterioration, which preserves the diagnostic utility of IgM serology in a disease that can kill within 48 h. VA-ECMO initiated at the first signs of cardiopulmonary decompensation has reported survival rates approaching 80% in selected experienced centers. No antiviral has demonstrated efficacy in controlled trials during the cardiopulmonary phase, and no licensed vaccine exists. Conclusions: HPS produces a mixed shock state through increased microvascular permeability, T cell-mediated immunopathology, and direct myocarditis. Management follows a stepwise algorithm: suspected HPS triggers immediate complete blood count with peripheral blood smear and concurrent hantavirus IgM serology and RT-PCR, followed by ICU admission, conservative fluid resuscitation guided by transpulmonary thermodilution, and early contact with an ECMO-capable center at the first sign of rising lactate, falling cardiac index, refractory shock, arrhythmia, or rapid oxygenation failure.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), a severe disease caused by New World orthohantaviruses such as Sin Nombre virus and Andes virus, characterized by rapidly progressive noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, myocardial depression, and high case fatality rates of 25% to 40%. The central question focuses on the mechanisms of cardiopulmonary failure, clinical recognition, and management strategies, particularly extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)-based interventions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis with emphasis on virological, pathophysiological, clinical, and therapeutic aspects of HCPS. Sources were identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, prioritizing original research articles, clinical series, and controlled trials published through 2025. Literature in English and Spanish was included.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Consensus supports that pathogenic hantaviruses enter endothelial cells and platelets via αvβ3 integrins, disrupting VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling and rendering endothelial cells hypersensitive to physiological VEGF concentrations. CD8+ T cell expansion and activated macrophages release TNF-alpha, IFN-gamma, and nitric oxide, amplifying microvascular permeability and contributing to myocardial depression. Autopsy studies confirm direct hantaviral myocarditis with viral antigen in cardiac endothelium and interstitial macrophages. Seroconversion precedes clinical deterioration, preserving the diagnostic utility of IgM serology.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: No antiviral has demonstrated efficacy in controlled trials during the cardiopulmonary phase, and no licensed vaccine exists. The review highlights heterogeneity in clinical presentations and the need for standardized diagnostic and management protocols, particularly regarding the timing of ECMO initiation and fluid resuscitation strategies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Immediate diagnostic algorithms are recommended: suspected HCPS should trigger complete blood count with peripheral blood smear, hantavirus IgM serology, and RT-PCR, followed by ICU admission, conservative fluid resuscitation guided by transpulmonary thermodilution, and early contact with an ECMO-capable center at the first sign of cardiopulmonary decompensation. Research priorities include evaluating antiviral efficacy during the cardiopulmonary phase and developing licensed vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes evidence on hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), a severe disease caused by New World orthohantaviruses such as Sin Nombre and Andes viruses, marked by rapid noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, myocardial depression, and high fatality rates. Mechanistically, hantaviruses disrupt VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling via αvβ3 integrins, while immune-mediated responses involving CD8+ T cells and macrophages amplify microvascular permeability and myocardial depression. Autopsy studies confirm direct viral myocarditis. Seroconversion precedes clinical deterioration, supporting IgM serology for early diagnosis. Management emphasizes immediate diagnostic workup, conservative fluid resuscitation guided by transpulmonary thermodilution, and early ECMO referral. Key gaps include the lack of effective antivirals and licensed vaccines, underscoring urgent research needs.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述检查了汉坦病毒心肺综合征(HCPS),这是一种由辛诺布尔病毒和安第斯病毒等新世界正汉坦病毒引起的严重疾病,其特征是快速进展的非心源性肺水肿、心肌抑制和25%至40%的高病死率。中心问题集中在心肺衰竭的机制、临床识别和管理策略,特别是基于体外膜氧合(ECMO)的干预措施。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇叙述性综合文章,重点关注 HCPS 的病毒学、病理生理学、临床和治疗方面。通过 PubMed、Scopus 和 Google Scholar 确定来源,优先考虑截至 2025 年发表的原创研究文章、临床系列和对照试验。其中包括英语和西班牙语文献。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 共识支持致病性汉坦病毒通过 αvβ3 整合素进入内皮细胞和血小板,破坏 VEGF-VEGFR2 信号传导并使内皮细胞对生理 VEGF 浓度过敏。CD8+ T 细胞扩增和活化的巨噬细胞释放 TNF-α、IFN-γ 和一氧化氮,增强微血管通透性并导致心肌抑制。尸检研究证实心脏内皮和间质巨噬细胞中存在病毒抗原,直接导致汉坦病毒性心肌炎。血清转化先于临床恶化,保留了 IgM 血清学 的诊断效用。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 抗病毒药物 尚未在心肺期的对照试验中证明其疗效,也不存在获得许可的 疫苗。该综述强调了临床表现的异质性以及标准化诊断和管理方案的必要性,特别是在 ECMO 启动时间和液体复苏策略方面。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 建议立即诊断算法:疑似 HCPS 应通过外周血涂片、汉坦病毒 IgM 血清学 和 RT-PCR 触发全血细胞计数,然后入住 ICU,在经肺热稀释指导下进行保守液体复苏,并在心肺失代偿的第一个迹象出现时尽早与具有 ECMO 能力的中心联系。研究重点包括评估 抗病毒药物 在心肺期的疗效以及开发获得许可的 疫苗。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS),也称为汉坦病毒心肺综合征,是由新世界汉坦病毒引起的,主要是北美的 Sin Nombre 病毒和南美的安第斯病毒。该综合征的特点是快速进展的非心源性肺水肿和心肌抑制,病死率为 25% 至 40%。南大西洋一艘探险游轮上的一艘2026年暴发病例,包括13例病例和3人死亡,证实安第斯山脉病毒可以在远离啮齿动物储存宿主的密闭环境中在人与人之间传播。方法:回顾了 HPS 的病毒学、病理生理学、临床和治疗方面,特别强调心肺机制。来源是通过 PubMed、Scopus 和 Google Scholar 确定的,优先考虑到 2025 年发表的原创研究文章、临床系列和对照试验。其中包括以英语和西班牙语发表的文献。结果:致病性汉坦病毒通过 αvβ3 整合素进入内皮细胞和血小板,破坏 VEGF-VEGFR2 信号轴并使内皮细胞对生理 VEGF 浓度过敏。CD8+ T 细胞的扩增和活化的巨噬细胞释放 TNF-α、IFN-γ 和一氧化氮,放大微血管通透性并导致心肌抑制。尸检研究表明,心脏内皮和间质巨噬细胞中存在病毒抗原,可导致直接汉坦病毒性心肌炎。经肺热稀​​释证实同时存在血容量不足、整体射血分数降低和血管外肺水升高。由于潜伏期长且心肺期基本上是免疫介导的,因此血清转化发生在临床恶化之前而不是之后,这保留了 IgM 血清学 在可在 48 小时内致死的疾病中的诊断效用。据报道,在选定的经验丰富的中心,在心肺失代偿的最初迹象出现时启动 VA-ECMO 的存活率接近 80%。抗病毒药物 尚未在心肺期的对照试验中证明其疗效,也不存在获得许可的 疫苗。结论:HPS 通过微血管通透性增加、T 细胞介导的免疫病理学和直接心肌炎产生混合休克状态。管理遵循逐步算法:疑似 HPS 立即通过外周血涂片和同时进行的汉坦病毒IgM 血清学 和 RT-PCR 进行全血细胞计数,然后入住 ICU,在经肺热稀释指导下进行保守性液体复苏,并在出现乳酸升高、心脏指数下降、难治性休克、心律失常或快速氧合衰竭的第一个迹象时尽早与具有 ECMO 能力的中心联系。

papers.title: Epidemiological characteristics and spatiotemporal heterogeneity of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in the Jiaodong Peninsula region, China, 2019–2025
papers.abstract: Background Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a serious zoonotic infectious disease. To characterize the spatiotemporal epidemiological patterns of HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula from 2019 to 2025 and to explore the influence of meteorological factors on its spatiotemporal heterogeneity, the present study conducted relevant analyses with the aim of providing evidence for the development of scientific and effective HFRS prevention and control measures. Method Data on HFRS were collected through the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention Information System. Descriptive epidemiology, Joinpoint regression analysis, spatial autocorrelation analysis, spatiotemporal clustering analysis and spatiotemporal geographically weighted regression model analysis were employed to examine the incidence of HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula region from 2019 to 2025. Result From 2019 to 2025, a total of 1,492 cases of HFRS were reported in the Jiaodong Peninsula region, with an average annual incidence rate of 1.073 per 100,000 people. The peak incidence period occurs annually from October to January of the following year. The age distribution is concentrated among those aged 45–74, with a male-to-female ratio of 2.58:1, and the occupational distribution is dominated by farmers. Overall, the spatial distribution pattern shows higher rates in the north and west compared to the south and east. Analysis using a join-point regression model indicates that the incidence rate showed an upward trend from 2019 to 2021, with an annual percentage change (APC) of 40.70% (95% CI: −15.72 to 134.88%, p = 0.103); however, this upward trend was not statistically significant. The incidence rate showed a downward trend from 2021 to 2025, with an APC of −13.60% (95% CI: −25.55 to 0.26%, p = 0.052); this downward trend was marginally significant. Analysis of global spatial autocorrelation revealed that, with the exception of 2019 (Moran’s I = 0.205, p = 0.052) and 2022 (Moran’s I = 0.189, p = 0.059), the incidence of HFRS showed spatial clustering in all other years (all with p < 0.05). Among these, 2021 had the highest agglomeration index (Moran’s I = 0.438). Analysis of local spatial autocorrelation shows that “high-high” clusters are primarily concentrated in the central and western parts of Yantai (around Laiyang, Haiyang, and Laizhou) and in the northern part of Qingdao (around Laixi). Spatio-temporal scanning analysis identified a total of three clusters, all concentrated in the fall and winter of 2021. The largest cluster spanned seven counties (cities and districts), primarily distributed across the inland and coastal areas of central and western Yantai (Laizhou, Zhaoyuan, Longkou, Laiyang, and Qixia) and northern Qingdao (Pingdu and Laixi). The Core Cluster scanning radius was 80.54 km. The high-incidence period was from November 1, 2021, to December 31, 2021. The Relative risk (RR) = 13.56, Log-likelihood ratio ((LLR) = 194.16, p < 0.01). GTWR model results demonstrated significant spatiotemporal heterogeneity of meteorological impacts on HFRS. Temperature showed an overall positive effect with a spatial pattern of west-strong and east-weak, south-high and north-low. Precipitation was positively associated with HFRS in eastern study areas but negatively in western areas, while relative humidity showed the opposite spatial pattern. Total solar radiation and wind speed exerted consistent negative inhibitory effects across the whole region, with wind speed presenting the strongest suppression. Atmospheric pressure mainly played a negative role, with only weak positive effects in partial southern Qingdao. Conclusion From 2019 to 2025, HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula region exhibited characteristics of seasonal prevalence, spatiotemporal clustering, and spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Health education should be strengthened among key populations, such as middle-aged and older male farmers, and prevention and control measures should be intensified in high-risk areas, including central-western Yantai and northern Qingdao. Future prevention and control strategies should incorporate region-specific climatic characteristics to formulate targeted interventions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a serious zoonotic infectious disease, and the study aimed to address gaps in understanding its spatiotemporal patterns and meteorological drivers in the Jiaodong Peninsula region of China.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed HFRS data collected through the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention Information System from 2019 to 2025 in the Jiaodong Peninsula region, employing descriptive epidemiology and advanced spatial-temporal modeling techniques.
analysis.methods: Descriptive epidemiology, Joinpoint regression analysis, spatial autocorrelation analysis, spatiotemporal clustering analysis, and a spatiotemporal geographically weighted regression (GTWR) model were used to examine HFRS incidence and its association with meteorological factors.
analysis.main_results: A total of 1,492 HFRS cases were reported from 2019 to 2025, with an average annual incidence rate of 1.073 per 100,000 people. The incidence showed an upward trend from 2019 to 2021 (APC 40.70%, p = 0.103) and a downward trend from 2021 to 2025 (APC −13.60%, p = 0.052). Spatial clustering was observed in most years, with the highest Moran’s I in 2021 (0.438). Three spatiotemporal clusters were identified, all concentrated in fall and winter of 2021, with the largest cluster spanning seven counties and a relative risk of 13.56.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interpreted HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula as exhibiting seasonal prevalence, spatiotemporal clustering, and meteorological heterogeneity, highlighting the need for region-specific prevention strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support targeted health education for high-risk groups such as middle-aged and older male farmers and intensified prevention in high-incidence areas like central-western Yantai and northern Qingdao.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of statistically significant trends in incidence changes and reliance on surveillance data without laboratory confirmation of hantavirus etiology.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized the epidemiology of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in the Jiaodong Peninsula, China, from 2019 to 2025, reporting 1,492 cases with an average annual incidence of 1.073 per 100,000. Incidence trends fluctuated, with a non-significant upward trend from 2019–2021 and a marginally significant downward trend from 2021–2025. Spatial clustering was evident in most years, peaking in 2021, and three spatiotemporal clusters were identified, all occurring in late 2021 with high relative risk. Meteorological factors showed heterogeneous effects, with temperature generally increasing risk, precipitation and humidity displaying opposite spatial patterns, and wind speed exerting strong suppression. The study concludes that HFRS exhibits seasonal prevalence, clustering, and meteorological heterogeneity, advocating for targeted prevention in high-risk areas and populations.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a serious zoonotic infectious disease, and the study aimed to address gaps in understanding its spatiotemporal patterns and meteorological drivers in the Jiaodong Peninsula region of China.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed HFRS data collected through the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention Information System from 2019 to 2025 in the Jiaodong Peninsula region, employing descriptive epidemiology and advanced spatial-temporal modeling techniques.
analysis_en.methods: Descriptive epidemiology, Joinpoint regression analysis, spatial autocorrelation analysis, spatiotemporal clustering analysis, and a spatiotemporal geographically weighted regression (GTWR) model were used to examine HFRS incidence and its association with meteorological factors.
analysis_en.main_results: A total of 1,492 HFRS cases were reported from 2019 to 2025, with an average annual incidence rate of 1.073 per 100,000 people. The incidence showed an upward trend from 2019 to 2021 (APC 40.70%, p = 0.103) and a downward trend from 2021 to 2025 (APC −13.60%, p = 0.052). Spatial clustering was observed in most years, with the highest Moran’s I in 2021 (0.438). Three spatiotemporal clusters were identified, all concentrated in fall and winter of 2021, with the largest cluster spanning seven counties and a relative risk of 13.56.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interpreted HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula as exhibiting seasonal prevalence, spatiotemporal clustering, and meteorological heterogeneity, highlighting the need for region-specific prevention strategies.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support targeted health education for high-risk groups such as middle-aged and older male farmers and intensified prevention in high-incidence areas like central-western Yantai and northern Qingdao.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of statistically significant trends in incidence changes and reliance on surveillance data without laboratory confirmation of hantavirus etiology.

papers.title_zh: 2019-2025年中国胶东半岛地区肾综合征出血热流行病学特征及时空异质性
papers.source_body_en: Background Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a serious zoonotic infectious disease. To characterize the spatiotemporal epidemiological patterns of HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula from 2019 to 2025 and to explore the influence of meteorological factors on its spatiotemporal heterogeneity, the present study conducted relevant analyses with the aim of providing evidence for the development of scientific and effective HFRS prevention and control measures. Method Data on HFRS were collected through the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention Information System. Descriptive epidemiology, Joinpoint regression analysis, spatial autocorrelation analysis, spatiotemporal clustering analysis and spatiotemporal geographically weighted regression model analysis were employed to examine the incidence of HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula region from 2019 to 2025. Result From 2019 to 2025, a total of 1,492 cases of HFRS were reported in the Jiaodong Peninsula region, with an average annual incidence rate of 1.073 per 100,000 people. The peak incidence period occurs annually from October to January of the following year. The age distribution is concentrated among those aged 45–74, with a male-to-female ratio of 2.58:1, and the occupational distribution is dominated by farmers. Overall, the spatial distribution pattern shows higher rates in the north and west compared to the south and east. Analysis using a join-point regression model indicates that the incidence rate showed an upward trend from 2019 to 2021, with an annual percentage change (APC) of 40.70% (95% CI: −15.72 to 134.88%, p = 0.103); however, this upward trend was not statistically significant. The incidence rate showed a downward trend from 2021 to 2025, with an APC of −13.60% (95% CI: −25.55 to 0.26%, p = 0.052); this downward trend was marginally significant. Analysis of global spatial autocorrelation revealed that, with the exception of 2019 (Moran’s I = 0.205, p = 0.052) and 2022 (Moran’s I = 0.189, p = 0.059), the incidence of HFRS showed spatial clustering in all other years (all with p < 0.05). Among these, 2021 had the highest agglomeration index (Moran’s I = 0.438). Analysis of local spatial autocorrelation shows that “high-high” clusters are primarily concentrated in the central and western parts of Yantai (around Laiyang, Haiyang, and Laizhou) and in the northern part of Qingdao (around Laixi). Spatio-temporal scanning analysis identified a total of three clusters, all concentrated in the fall and winter of 2021. The largest cluster spanned seven counties (cities and districts), primarily distributed across the inland and coastal areas of central and western Yantai (Laizhou, Zhaoyuan, Longkou, Laiyang, and Qixia) and northern Qingdao (Pingdu and Laixi). The Core Cluster scanning radius was 80.54 km. The high-incidence period was from November 1, 2021, to December 31, 2021. The Relative risk (RR) = 13.56, Log-likelihood ratio ((LLR) = 194.16, p < 0.01). GTWR model results demonstrated significant spatiotemporal heterogeneity of meteorological impacts on HFRS. Temperature showed an overall positive effect with a spatial pattern of west-strong and east-weak, south-high and north-low. Precipitation was positively associated with HFRS in eastern study areas but negatively in western areas, while relative humidity showed the opposite spatial pattern. Total solar radiation and wind speed exerted consistent negative inhibitory effects across the whole region, with wind speed presenting the strongest suppression. Atmospheric pressure mainly played a negative role, with only weak positive effects in partial southern Qingdao. Conclusion From 2019 to 2025, HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula region exhibited characteristics of seasonal prevalence, spatiotemporal clustering, and spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Health education should be strengthened among key populations, such as middle-aged and older male farmers, and prevention and control measures should be intensified in high-risk areas, including central-western Yantai and northern Qingdao. Future prevention and control strategies should incorporate region-specific climatic characteristics to formulate targeted interventions.

papers.title: Emerging infectious diseases (Mpox, Nipah, and Andes): A narrative review of transmission, environmental survival, and disinfection
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus are emerging infectious diseases that cause outbreaks associated with nosocomial transmission. METHODS: This narrative review summarizes the Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment with a focus on environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention. RESULTS: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus all survive in the environment and are capable of indirect transmission. All these viruses are enveloped and susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants. CONCLUSIONS: Rapid identification of patients with known or suspected infections of these emerging viruses coupled with adherence to infection prevention recommendations will prevent healthcare-associated transmission.

papers.title: The Wellness-Risk Paradox at Sea: Wellness Positioning, Outbreak Exposure and Health-Quality Assurance in the Cruise Sector
papers.abstract: ‘Wellness-at-sea’ is an integral part of the cruise holiday service bundle. Marketed within an image of experiential diversity within a safe, controlled environment, it features medical centers, spa facilities and restoration-focused itineraries. Nevertheless, epidemiologically speaking, cruise ships rank amongst the riskiest transmission environments in tourism. This perspective paper proposes a typology of wellness cruising along two axes (i.e., offer scope: themed voyages versus onboard amenities and promotion focus: borrowed credibility versus narrative ‘storyscaping’) and uses it to develop the ‘wellness-risk paradox’, a boundary case for health-tourism literature. Three testable propositions emerge: reputational risk exposure increases with the offer’s wellness centrality; narrative-based promotion is more susceptible than credibility-based promotion and a quadrant-adjusted health-assurance scheme is more effective than current inspection standards. The argument draws on the 2026 Andes hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius (three deaths among thirteen cases), the 2020 Diamond Princess outbreak, and a decade of official outbreak surveillance, reporting an increase in gastrointestinal outbreaks from 0.34 to 0.62 per million passengers between 2019 and 2025 (rate ratio 1.84, 95% CI 0.87–3.86), which reverses the pre-pandemic downward trend although annual counts remain too small for the change to reach conventional statistical significance. Sanitation-inspection compliance cannot reliably predict outbreaks, nor does it facilitate trust. Four domains of action are proposed: continuous air-quality monitoring, wastewater surveillance, behavioral risk modeling and jurisdictional coordination.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a perspective paper that does not conduct a systematic review or meta-analysis. It draws on case studies and historical data, including the 2026 Andes hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius, the 2020 Diamond Princess outbreak, and a decade of official outbreak surveillance. The paper outlines a typology of wellness cruising and proposes a framework for understanding the wellness-risk paradox.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that cruise ships, despite their wellness positioning, are among the riskiest environments for disease transmission. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that sanitation-inspection compliance is not a reliable predictor of outbreaks and does not facilitate trust. It also identifies a gap in the ability to accurately assess the effectiveness of current inspection standards compared to proposed quadrant-adjusted health-assurance schemes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes four domains for action: continuous air-quality monitoring, wastewater surveillance, behavioral risk modeling, and jurisdictional coordination. analysis.summary_en: This review examines the paradox of wellness positioning in the cruise sector and its implications for disease transmission, particularly focusing on hantaviruses. It highlights how cruise ships, despite being marketed as safe and wellness-oriented environments, are among the riskiest for outbreaks. The paper uses case studies, including the 2026 Andes hantavirus outbreak and the 2020 Diamond Princess outbreak, to illustrate the tension between wellness promotion and outbreak risks. It argues that current sanitation-inspection compliance is insufficient for predicting or preventing outbreaks and proposes four domains for action: air-quality monitoring, wastewater surveillance, behavioral risk modeling, and jurisdictional coordination. The review emphasizes the need for a more integrated approach to health-quality assurance in the cruise industry.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该评论探讨了邮轮行业健康定位的悖论及其对 暴发 传播 和健康质量保证的影响。它重点关注汉坦病毒及其相关综合症,研究以健康为中心的邮轮环境如何可能无意中增加 传播 疾病的风险,尽管它们在市场上是安全的。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇观点论文,不进行系统综述或荟萃分析。它借鉴了案例研究和历史数据,包括 MV Hondius 上的 2026 年安第斯山脉汉坦病毒暴发、2020 年钻石公主号 暴发 以及官方 暴发 监测 的十年。该论文概述了健康巡航的类型,并提出了一个理解健康风险悖论的框架。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,尽管游轮处于健康定位,但它仍然是疾病 传播 风险最高的环境之一。它强调需要更细致地了解健康促进如何与 暴发 风险相互作用,并表明当前的卫生检查合规性无法可靠地预测或预防 暴发。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,卫生检查合规性并不是 暴发 的可靠预测因素,并且不利于信任。它还确定了与拟议的象限调整健康保障计划相比,准确评估当前检查标准有效性的能力存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查提出了四个行动领域:持续空气质量监测、废水 监测、行为风险建模和管辖协调。建议将这些领域作为改善邮轮行业健康质量保证和 暴发 预防的优先事项。

news.content: Social Media Links Facebook Twitter Instagram YouTube Rss Podcast whatsapp Search Close Start Date to End Date Select Type Select Type News Listen News Regional Bulletins Bulletins Detail News Programmes Special Programs Mann ki Baat From Archives Circulars RTI Replies Vacancies Regional Units Detail Download Mobile App Language Selection Englishहिन्दीमराठीગુજરાતીUrduDogriAssameseRajasthaniবাংলা Menu News On AIR International Regional News Business Sports Miscellaneous Archives Audios: News & Current Affairs Transcripts News in Regional Languages (Audios & Text) Text Archive Search Listen News Evening News Mann Ki Baat Screen Reader Access Prev Play/Pause Next 00:00 % buffered 00:00 Unmute Mute Transcript summary Play Audio Evening News Home International Hantavirus outbreak forces cruise passengers to leave ship at St Helena News On AIR | May 7, 2026 5:13 PM Hantavirus outbreak forces cruise passengers to leave ship at St Helena Around 40 passengers from a cruise ship hit by a deadly hantavirus outbreak disembarked at the remote South Atlantic island of St Helena last month without contact tracing, nearly two weeks after the first passenger died on board. The Dutch Foreign Ministry has confirmed the number. It comes as international authorities intensify efforts to contain a rare outbreak of deadly disease linked to the Andes strain of hantavirus after three people who were aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius have died since it set sail from Argentina a month ago. The Dutch-flagged expedition vessel, carrying around 150 passengers and crew from 23 different countries, is now sailing towards Spain’s Canary Islands under strict precautionary measures after being anchored for three days near Cape Verde, an archipelago nation off the West African coast. The ship operator company, Oceanwide Expeditions, had previously said the body of the Dutch man who died on the 11th of April was taken off the ship at the island of St Helena, where his wife also disembarked. She then flew to South Africa and died there. The company had not previously acknowledged that dozens more people left the ship at that time. The company said the people who left the ship to return to their home countries were of at least 12 different nationalities. Meanwhile, two passengers in serious condition have arrived in the Netherlands for treatment after being evacuated from the cruise ship. A third passenger, reported to be in stable condition, remains aboard a delayed evacuation flight. The three suspected hantavirus patients of British, Dutch and German nationalities were transferred by medical evacuation teams in full hazmat gear, including respirators, gowns and face shields, from the cruise ship into specialised air ambulances near Amsterdam and Cape Verde this week. The World Health Organisation said the outbreak likely involves the Andes strain of hantavirus – the only known strain capable of limited human-to-human transmission through close contact. Authorities in Europe, South Africa and Argentina are continuing contact tracing, quarantine planning and laboratory testing to contain the outbreak. Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome is usually transmitted through inhalation of aerosolised rodent urine, saliva or droppings. However, the Andes strain circulating in parts of Argentina and Chile has previously shown limited person-to-person transmission, particularly among close household contacts. news.content: Feedback | Thursday, August 20, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports Commonwealth Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories Two suspected hantavirus cases found in Spain, remote Tristan da Cunha 09/05/26 | 12:29 pm | Hanta virus | Spain | Tristan da Cunha Share Your browser does not support JavaScript Two suspected hantavirus cases found in Spain, remote Tristan da Cunha Health experts raced to contain a potential spread of hantavirus as two suspected cases emerged on Friday far from the luxury cruise liner where the outbreak started. The latest reports involved a man who fell ill after leaving the ship and a woman who became sick after sitting near an infected cruise passenger on a plane. The occurrences reported by health officials thousands of miles apart — one in Spain, the other on the remote South Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha — are separate from the World Health Organization’s tally of eight people who became ill aboard the Dutch-flagged ship MV Hondius. Three of those people have died. WHO officials said on Friday six of the eight suspected cases have been confirmed as hantavirus, a potentially fatal disease typically carried and spread by rodents. CRUISE SHIP BOUND FOR CANARY ISLANDS The announcements of new cases far from the vessel fuelled concern about a wider spread of the virus, although WHO officials have repeatedly said the risk to the public at large is not high and the virus is not transmitted easily. “Based on the dynamics of this outbreak, based on how it is spreading and not spreading amongst the people on the ship, the people who have disembarked, as well, we continue to consider the risk as low for the general population,” Anais Legand, WHO technical officer for viral threats, said in an online briefing. Testing has determined that the Hondius outbreak, the first of its kind documented on a ship, involves the Andes virus, the only hantavirus species known to be capable of limited transmission between humans, through close and prolonged contact, according to the WHO. The U.N. health body puts the fatality rates among infected people in the United States at up to 50%. The ship was carrying 147 passengers and crew when a cluster of severe respiratory illnesses among passengers was first reported to the WHO on Sunday. By then, 34 other passengers had departed the vessel, which first sailed from Argentina in March with stops in the Antarctic and other locations before heading north to waters off Cape Verde west of Africa. The vessel was briefly held there this week after news of the outbreak emerged. Four patients remained hospitalized on Friday in South Africa, the Netherlands and Switzerland. Oceanwide, the cruise operator, said on Thursday there were no people with symptoms of a possible infection remaining on the vessel. The Hondius was en route on Friday to Tenerife in the Canary Islands, and was expected to dock there early on Sunday. Arriving passengers and crew will be screened before disembarking under guidelines still being finalised by the WHO and other health agencies. Oceanwide said 17 U.S. citizens were aboard. Health officials will meet passengers returning to the United States and transport them on a “medical repatriation flight” to Omaha, where they will be quarantined at the University of Nebraska, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said on Friday. STRANGERS ON A PLANE A 32-year-old woman in the southeastern Spanish province of Alicante was diagnosed with symptoms consistent with a hantavirus infection and was being tested, Spanish health authorities said. She was briefly sitting on a plane two rows behind a Dutch woman who had contracted the virus on the Hondius, Spanish Secretary of State for Health Javier Padilla told reporters. The woman left the flight in Johannesburg feeling ill before it took off on April 25 and later died at a hospital. A British man was suspected of having the disease on Britain’s Tristan da Cunha, the nation’s Health Security Agency said. Officials said he was a passenger on the Hondius, which was at the island from April 13 to April 15. The three people who have died following the outbreak were a Dutch couple and a German national. Four others confirmed to be infected — two Britons, a Dutch person and a Swiss national — were still being treated at hospitals in the Netherlands, South Africa and Switzerland. Britain’s Health Security Agency did not go into further detail about the British passenger on Tristan da Cunha identified with suspected symptoms. But the case illustrated how infectious diseases could potentially spread far in the era of modern travel. Tristan da Cunha, home to only around 200 people, is halfway between South Africa and South America. It is the world’s remotest inhabited island, more than 1,500 miles (2,400 km) and a six-day boat ride from St Helena, its nearest inhabited neighbour. The Spanish woman has “mild respiratory symptoms” and had been to a hospital where she would be tested for the virus, according to a statement on the regional health department’s website. The CDC has classified the hantavirus outbreak as a “level 3” emergency response, the lowest level of emergency activation. Other experts have stressed the low probability of a widespread contagion, but the outbreak has put authorities on high alert as they urge all who have been in contact with passengers who left the Hondius to watch out for possible symptoms. news.content_original: Feedback | Thursday, August 20, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports Commonwealth Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories Two suspected hantavirus cases found in Spain, remote Tristan da Cunha 09/05/26 | 12:29 pm | Hanta virus | Spain | Tristan da Cunha Share Your browser does not support JavaScript Two suspected hantavirus cases found in Spain, remote Tristan da Cunha Health experts raced to contain a potential spread of hantavirus as two suspected cases emerged on Friday far from the luxury cruise liner where the outbreak started. The latest reports involved a man who fell ill after leaving the ship and a woman who became sick after sitting near an infected cruise passenger on a plane. The occurrences reported by health officials thousands of miles apart — one in Spain, the other on the remote South Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha — are separate from the World Health Organization’s tally of eight people who became ill aboard the Dutch-flagged ship MV Hondius. Three of those people have died. WHO officials said on Friday six of the eight suspected cases have been confirmed as hantavirus, a potentially fatal disease typically carried and spread by rodents. CRUISE SHIP BOUND FOR CANARY ISLANDS The announcements of new cases far from the vessel fuelled concern about a wider spread of the virus, although WHO officials have repeatedly said the risk to the public at large is not high and the virus is not transmitted easily. “Based on the dynamics of this outbreak, based on how it is spreading and not spreading amongst the people on the ship, the people who have disembarked, as well, we continue to consider the risk as low for the general population,” Anais Legand, WHO technical officer for viral threats, said in an online briefing. Testing has determined that the Hondius outbreak, the first of its kind documented on a ship, involves the Andes virus, the only hantavirus species known to be capable of limited transmission between humans, through close and prolonged contact, according to the WHO. The U.N. health body puts the fatality rates among infected people in the United States at up to 50%. The ship was carrying 147 passengers and crew when a cluster of severe respiratory illnesses among passengers was first reported to the WHO on Sunday. By then, 34 other passengers had departed the vessel, which first sailed from Argentina in March with stops in the Antarctic and other locations before heading north to waters off Cape Verde west of Africa. The vessel was briefly held there this week after news of the outbreak emerged. Four patients remained hospitalized on Friday in South Africa, the Netherlands and Switzerland. Oceanwide, the cruise operator, said on Thursday there were no people with symptoms of a possible infection remaining on the vessel. The Hondius was en route on Friday to Tenerife in the Canary Islands, and was expected to dock there early on Sunday. Arriving passengers and crew will be screened before disembarking under guidelines still being finalised by the WHO and other health agencies. Oceanwide said 17 U.S. citizens were aboard. Health officials will meet passengers returning to the United States and transport them on a “medical repatriation flight” to Omaha, where they will be quarantined at the University of Nebraska, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said on Friday. STRANGERS ON A PLANE A 32-year-old woman in the southeastern Spanish province of Alicante was diagnosed with symptoms consistent with a hantavirus infection and was being tested, Spanish health authorities said. She was briefly sitting on a plane two rows behind a Dutch woman who had contracted the virus on the Hondius, Spanish Secretary of State for Health Javier Padilla told reporters. The woman left the flight in Johannesburg feeling ill before it took off on April 25 and later died at a hospital. A British man was suspected of having the disease on Britain’s Tristan da Cunha, the nation’s Health Security Agency said. Officials said he was a passenger on the Hondius, which was at the island from April 13 to April 15. The three people who have died following the outbreak were a Dutch couple and a German national. Four others confirmed to be infected — two Britons, a Dutch person and a Swiss national — were still being treated at hospitals in the Netherlands, South Africa and Switzerland. Britain’s Health Security Agency did not go into further detail about the British passenger on Tristan da Cunha identified with suspected symptoms. But the case illustrated how infectious diseases could potentially spread far in the era of modern travel. Tristan da Cunha, home to only around 200 people, is halfway between South Africa and South America. It is the world’s remotest inhabited island, more than 1,500 miles (2,400 km) and a six-day boat ride from St Helena, its nearest inhabited neighbour. The Spanish woman has “mild respiratory symptoms” and had been to a hospital where she would be tested for the virus, according to a statement on the regional health department’s website. The CDC has classified the hantavirus outbreak as a “level 3” emergency response, the lowest level of emergency activation. Other experts have stressed the low probability of a widespread contagion, but the outbreak has put authorities on high alert as they urge all who have been in contact with passengers who left the Hondius to watch out for possible symptoms. French Health Minister Stephanie Rist confirmed this today. The woman was among five French nationals evacuated from the cruise ship and repatriated to France yesterday, developing symptoms during the repatriation flight. Rist said the woman’s condition worsened overnight, and she was transferred to a specialised infectious disease hospital for treatment. The minister also announced that 22 close contacts of Hantavirus cases had been identified in France and ordered to isolate. Earlier, French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu had said the five French passengers who arrived in France yesterday afternoon aboard a medical evacuation flight were immediately placed under strict isolation until further notice. But while it was serious, the WHO said it assesses the public health risk as low. WHO has now informed the 12 countries whose nationals disembarked the cruise ship MV Hondius earlier during the voyage at the remote British territory of Saint Helena in the South Atlantic Ocean. Those 12 countries are Canada, Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Singapore, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkyie, the United Kingdom and the United States of America. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, said in a media briefing in Geneva that the agency currently expects the outbreak to remain limited if appropriate public health measures are implemented quickly and effectively. He, however, warned that additional cases remain possible as authorities continue tracing exposed passengers and contacts across multiple countries. WHO said around 2,500 hantavirus diagnostic kits are being shipped from laboratories in Argentina to five countries. The Dutch Foreign Ministry has confirmed that around 40 passengers from the cruise ship hit by a deadly hantavirus outbreak disembarked at the island of St. Helena. OffOn Stream on 3 people waiting to be medically evacuated from cruise ship at center of suspected hantavirus outbreak There are currently two laboratory-confirmed and five suspected cases. ByMary Kekatos and Othon Leyva May 6, 2026, 1:06 AM At least three people are waiting to be medically evacuated from a cruise ship at the center of a suspected hantavirus outbreak. As of Monday, there have been seven cases reported aboard the MV Hondius, of which two are laboratory-confirmed and five are suspected. Among those seven, there have been three deaths, including a married couple from the Netherlands, one of whom has been confirmed to have been infected with hantavirus. The ship is currently off the coast of Cape Verde and medical teams have been assessing two staff members and a close contact of one of the deceased patients. Related American speaks out from cruise ship amid deadly hantavirus outbreak Cape Verde officials told ABC News they are checking on what care the three patients need before transferring them to ambulances and then on flights to the Netherlands. Two planes have been arranged for medical evacuations of the sick passengers from the ship between 4 a.m. and 6 a.m. ET, according to World Health Organization representative for Cape Verde Dr. Ann Lindstrand. The vessel is expected to sail to the Spanish island of Tenerife in Spain, where Spanish health authorities will take over further investigations, including lab testing and clinical assessments, particularly for older passengers, according to Cape Verde officials. Jake Rosmarin, an American passenger on the ship, told ABC News that all the remaining passengers on board remain "in good spirits" and "are hopeful that this situation will be resolved soon." "Safety measures are in place, including social distancing and masking. Passengers also have the option to have meals delivered directly to their cabins," he said. "Access to the outer decks is permitted for fresh air, while gathering in indoor common areas such as the lounge is currently restricted." This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 5, 2026. AFP via Getty Images It comes as an epidemiologist at the WHO said there may be some person-to-person spread in the outbreak. "We do believe that there may be some human-to-human transmission that's happening among the really close contacts, the husband and wife, people who've shared cabins, [et cetera]," Maria Van Kerkhove, an infectious disease epidemiologist and director of Epidemic and Pandemic Management at the WHO, said during a press conference Tuesday. "So again, our assumption is that has happened, and that's why we are operating and working with the ship to make sure that anyone who is symptomatic, anyone caring for patients, is wearing full personal protective equipment," she added. Van Kerkhove noted that hantaviruses normally don't transmit from person to person because it's a "rodent infection." Patients typically become infected when they come into contact with rodent urine, droppings or saliva, according to the WHO. The initial patients who fell ill may have become infected before they boarded the ship, Van Kerkhove added. Symptoms of hantavirus infections sometimes do not start until eight weeks after contact with the virus, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Related 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know The WHO is working under the assumption that the strain of hantavirus in the suspected outbreak is the Andes virus, which historically has been shown to potentially transmit between people, although sequencing is still ongoing, according to Van Kerkhove. In a post on its website, the WHO said the onset of illnesses aboard the MV Hondius occurred between April 6 and April 28, with patients experiencing fever, gastrointestinal symptoms, rapid progression to pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome and shock. "The outbreak is being managed through coordinated international response, and includes in-depth investigations, case isolation and care, medical evacuation and laboratory investigations," the WHO wrote in the post. WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Ghebreysus wrote in a post on X Tuesday that the infection risk to the global population is low and that the agency will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates. Timeline of cases The first suspected hantavirus case occurred in a 70-year-old male passenger from the Netherlands who developed fever, headache and mild diarrhea on April 6, according to the WHO and South African health officials. Popular Reads Actress Hayden Panettiere dies at 36, found in cardiac arrest Aug 17 Iran live updates: Araghchi dismisses Trump's 'economic D-Day' threat 5 hours ago Jared Kushner traveling in Egypt and Israel this week Aug 16 On April 11, the passenger developed respiratory distress and died on board the ship the same day. His body was removed from the ship to the British territory of St. Helena on April 24. No microbiological tests were performed on the man, according to the WHO. Also on April 24, the male passenger's 69-year-old wife developed gastrointestinal symptoms, health officials said. Her health rapidly declined while on a flight to Johannesburg, South Africa, on April 25 and she died upon arrival to an emergency department the next day, the WHO said. WHO epidemic and pandemic preparedness and prevention chief Maria Van Kerkhove speaking regarding hantavirus cases at the WHO heaquarters in Geneva, May 4, 2026. World Health Organization/AFP via Getty Images On Monday, May 4, laboratory testing confirmed that the wife was infected with hantavirus. Health workers have begun working to identify anyone who may have come into contact with the couple. According to the WHO, the couple had traveled in South America, including Argentina, before they boarded the cruise ship on April 1. During Tuesday's press conference, Van Kerkhove said officials suspect the couple was infected with hantavirus before boarding the ship. "The initial patients, the initial case and his wife, they joined the boat in Argentina. And with the timing of the incubation period of hantavirus, which can be anywhere from one to six weeks, our assumption is that they were infected off the ship, perhaps doing some activities there," she said. A British passenger started developing symptoms on April 24, including shortness of breath and signs of pneumonia, according to the WHO and South African health officials. His condition worsened and he was medically evacuated from Ascension, another British territory, to South Africa on April 27, where he is currently hospitalized in an intensive care unit. Laboratory testing confirmed hantavirus infection over the weekend, the WHO said. Another passenger, an adult female, began experiencing symptoms on April 28, including a general feeling of being unwell, according to the WHO. She later presented with pneumonia and died on May 2. Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates the cruise ship, previously revealed that the patient was a German national. In addition, there are three suspected cases currently onboard the MV Hondius reporting high fever and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, the WHO said. The ship is currently off the coast of Cape Verde, where medical teams in the area are evaluating the patients and collecting additional specimens for testing, according to the WHO. Van Kerkhove said the highest priority is to medically evacuate the symptomatic individuals onboard the ship so they receive the care they need. "The plan now is for the ship to continue on to the Canary Islands. We're working with Spanish authorities who will welcome the ship, have said that they will welcome the ship, to do a full investigation, a full epidemiological investigation, full disinfection of the ship, and of course to assess the risk of the passengers that are actually on board," she said. "The medical evacuation of two individuals currently requiring urgent medical care, and the individual associated with the guest who passed away on 2 May, will occur using two specialized aircraft that are en route to Cape Verde," Oceanwide Expeditions said in a statement Tuesday. "From here, the patients are to be medically evacuated to the Netherlands," the statement continued, noting that there currently was no "exact timeline" for the evacuation. The company added that once the guests have been safely transferred and are in transit to the Netherlands, the ship will proceed to the Canary Islands. "[T]he hospital has already prepared an area with isolation capacity, should it be necessary," Angela Gomes, Cape Verde's national director of health, said in a statement Tuesday. "A dedicated team has been formed, with doctors, infectious disease specialists, nurses and laboratory technicians, to support patients on board and, if necessary, also on land." The Spanish Ministry of Health said Spain will host the MV Hondius vessel in the Canary Islands in compliance with "international law and the humanitarian spirit." Once there, crew and passengers will be examined, treated and transferred to their respective countries, the ministry said. Following this same logic, and as part of the operation, the Government has also accepted a formal request from the Government of the Netherlands to take in the doctor from the MV Hondius, who is in serious condition and will be transported to the Canary Islands on a hospital plane today. ABC News' Emily Cohen and Dada Jovanovic contributed to this report. Also on April 24, the male passenger's 69-year-old wife developed gastrointestinal symptoms, health officials said. Her health rapidly declined while on a flight to Johannesburg, South Africa, on April 25 and she died upon arrival to an emergency department the next day, the WHO said. WHO epidemic and pandemic preparedness and prevention chief Maria Van Kerkhove speaking regarding hantavirus cases at the WHO heaquarters in Geneva, May 4, 2026. World Health Organization/AFP via Getty Images On Monday, May 4, laboratory testing confirmed that the wife was infected with hantavirus. Health workers have begun working to identify anyone who may have come into contact with the couple. According to the WHO, the couple had traveled in South America, including Argentina, before they boarded the cruise ship on April 1. During Tuesday's press conference, Van Kerkhove said officials suspect the couple was infected with hantavirus before boarding the ship. "The initial patients, the initial case and his wife, they joined the boat in Argentina. And with the timing of the incubation period of hantavirus, which can be anywhere from one to six weeks, our assumption is that they were infected off the ship, perhaps doing some activities there," she said. A British passenger started developing symptoms on April 24, including shortness of breath and signs of pneumonia, according to the WHO and South African health officials. His condition worsened and he was medically evacuated from Ascension, another British territory, to South Africa on April 27, where he is currently hospitalized in an intensive care unit. Laboratory testing confirmed hantavirus infection over the weekend, the WHO said. Another passenger, an adult female, began experiencing symptoms on April 28, including a general feeling of being unwell, according to the WHO. She later presented with pneumonia and died on May 2. Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates the cruise ship, previously revealed that the patient was a German national. In addition, there are three suspected cases currently onboard the MV Hondius reporting high fever and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, the WHO said. The ship is currently off the coast of Cape Verde, where medical teams in the area are evaluating the patients and collecting additional specimens for testing, according to the WHO. Van Kerkhove said the highest priority is to medically evacuate the symptomatic individuals onboard the ship so they receive the care they need. "The plan now is for the ship to continue on to the Canary Islands. We're working with Spanish authorities who will welcome the ship, have said that they will welcome the ship, to do a full investigation, a full epidemiological investigation, full disinfection of the ship, and of course to assess the risk of the passengers that are actually on board," she said. "The medical evacuation of two individuals currently requiring urgent medical care, and the individual associated with the guest who passed away on 2 May, will occur using two specialized aircraft that are en route to Cape Verde," Oceanwide Expeditions said in a statement Tuesday. "From here, the patients are to be medically evacuated to the Netherlands," the statement continued, noting that there currently was no "exact timeline" for the evacuation. The company added that once the guests have been safely transferred and are in transit to the Netherlands, the ship will proceed to the Canary Islands. "[T]he hospital has already prepared an area with isolation capacity, should it be necessary," Angela Gomes, Cape Verde's national director of health, said in a statement Tuesday. "A dedicated team has been formed, with doctors, infectious disease specialists, nurses and laboratory technicians, to support patients on board and, if necessary, also on land." The Spanish Ministry of Health said Spain will host the MV Hondius vessel in the Canary Islands in compliance with "international law and the humanitarian spirit." Once there, crew and passengers will be examined, treated and transferred to their respective countries, the ministry said. Following this same logic, and as part of the operation, the Government has also accepted a formal request from the Government of the Netherlands to take in the doctor from the MV Hondius, who is in serious condition and will be transported to the Canary Islands on a hospital plane today. ABC News' Emily Cohen and Dada Jovanovic contributed to this report.
